citeAs: Jian Xie, Kai Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Tinghui Zhu, Renze Lou, Yuandong Tian, Yanghua Xiao, Yu Su (2024). TravelPlanner: A Benchmark for Real-World Planning with Language Agents. arXiv:2402.01622.
creator: Jian Xie, Kai Zhang, Jiangjie Chen, Tinghui Zhu, Renze Lou, Yuandong Tian, Yanghua Xiao, Yu Su (Fudan University, The Ohio State University, The Pennsylvania State University, Meta AI)
description: TravelPlanner is a planning benchmark focused on travel planning that provides a rich sandbox environment with around four million data entries crawled from the Internet, accessible via six tools. It includes 1,225 meticulously curated diverse user queries along with their reference plans, each imposing a different combination of constraints (environment, commonsense, and hard constraints). The benchmark evaluates whether language agents can develop flexible travel plans by collecting information via diverse tools and making decisions while satisfying multiple constraints.
name: TravelPlanner
publisher: OSU NLP Group (The Ohio State University)
rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 (one human-annotated reference plan per query; the paper states "we ensure the high quality of each query in TravelPlanner and the presence of at least one feasible solution")
rai:annotatorDemographics: 20 graduate students (specific nationality, gender, or other demographic details not provided).
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Custom annotation process; annotators were 20 graduate students who manually annotated plans and were paid an average of $0.80 per plan. No third-party crowdsourcing platform mentioned.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: 20 graduate students were invited to meticulously annotate plans for synthesized queries. A plan was deemed eligible only if it met all the constraints outlined in the evaluation script. Annotators were paid an average of $0.80 for each plan they annotated. The authors performed a detailed review of every query and plan, rectifying any errors found. Budget was re-calibrated using costs from corresponding human-annotated plans to ensure challenge level.
rai:dataBiases: A static and closed sandbox environment was deliberately created to avoid variability and potential biases introduced by dynamic data, ensuring all agents access the same unchanging information. Original data was modified (keys and values added, deleted, altered) to avoid data contamination. Budget values were re-calibrated using human-annotated plan costs to replace heuristic-generated budgets that might be too high, thereby reducing the number of feasible plans and ensuring challenge level.
rai:dataCollection: The dataset environment was constructed from multiple sources: FlightSearch data was sourced from the Kaggle Flight Status Prediction dataset (spanning 2022-03-01 to 2022-04-01); DistanceMatrix data was obtained via the Google Distance Matrix API; RestaurantSearch data was sourced from the Kaggle Zomato Restaurants Dataset; AttractionSearch data was gathered using the Google Places API; AccommodationSearch data was obtained from the Kaggle Airbnb Open Data Dataset. The original data was then modified (adding, deleting, and altering certain keys and values) to suit benchmark requirements and avoid data contamination. Queries were constructed by randomly selecting departure city, destination, date range, travel duration, and hard constraints, then using GPT-4 to generate natural language queries. Reference plans were annotated by 20 graduate students.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data sources include: (1) Kaggle Flight Status Prediction dataset for flight information; (2) Google Distance Matrix API for driving distances and travel times between cities; (3) Kaggle Zomato Restaurants Dataset for restaurant names and average costs; (4) Google Places API for attraction information; (5) Kaggle Airbnb Open Data Dataset for accommodation details including room type, price, minimum nights, review rate, and maximum occupancy.
rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Flight data spans from 2022-03-01 to 2022-04-01. The sandbox environment uses data based on the year 2022.
rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Manual Human Curator, Secondary Data analysis
rai:dataLimitations: The evaluation criteria for commonsense constraints are based on the authors' consensus, which may not capture all definitions of commonsense. The sandbox is static and closed, which may not fully reflect the dynamic nature of real-world travel planning. The dataset uses data from 2022, which may not reflect current travel options. The benchmark strictly prohibits any form of cheating in the validation and test sets.
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Original data from each source was modified to avoid data contamination: keys and values were added, deleted, and altered. Price fields were synthetically generated (e.g., flight prices computed by multiplying distance by a random factor of 0.2–0.5; driving/taxi costs computed by multiplying distance by factors of 1 and 0.15 respectively). Restaurants were randomly assigned to cities and randomly categorized under cuisine types. Accommodations were randomly assigned to cities and given random room rules. A static, closed sandbox environment was created to ensure consistent and unbiased evaluations.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Original data from each source was modified by adding, deleting, and altering certain keys and values to suit benchmark requirements and avoid data contamination. For FlightSearch, fields like FlightDate, DepTime, ArrTime, ActualElapsedTime, Distance, OriginCityName, and DestCityName were retained while others were discarded; Price was generated by multiplying Distance by a random factor ranging from 0.2 to 0.5. For RestaurantSearch, restaurants were randomly assigned to various cities and randomly categorized under cuisine types. For AccommodationSearch, items were randomly assigned to cities and given random room rules. For AttractionSearch, search results were stored in a standardized database. Budget values were re-calibrated using costs from human-annotated plans to replace heuristic-generated budgets.
rai:dataSocialImpact: TravelPlanner aims to provide an effective benchmark for complex planning in future research. Some data in the TravelPlanner environment is derived from publicly available data on the Internet, and the content does not represent the authors' viewpoints. The authors acknowledge that definitions of commonsense may differ across individuals and encourage additional discussions to enrich the commonsense dimension. The benchmark could contribute to developing language agents capable of automating tedious planning tasks for humans.
rai:dataUseCases: TravelPlanner is intended as a benchmark for evaluating language agents on complex real-world planning tasks involving tool use, multi-constraint satisfaction, and long-horizon decision making. It is designed to test agents' capabilities in: (1) tool use to collect information from a partially observable environment, (2) satisfying multiple simultaneous constraints (environment, commonsense, and hard/user-specified constraints), and (3) delivering complete and feasible multi-day travel plans. It also supports training via reinforcement learning using evaluation feedback on the training set.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4 was used to generate natural language queries from structured JSON elements. GPT-4-Turbo was used to extract key components (transportation, restaurants, attractions, accommodations) from natural language plans into structured JSON format for evaluation.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: No personal or sensitive information is collected. The dataset consists of synthetic travel queries and plans based on publicly available travel data (flights, restaurants, attractions, accommodations). No user personal data is included.
